proposals.entity_key: Placement of short adverbs in passé composé
value: Short adverbs (beaucoup, trop, assez, bien, souvent, toujours) are invariable and never agree with the subject.
Past participle agreement is unchanged: with être it agrees with the subject, with avoir with a preceding direct object.

evidence.notes: Adverbs are invariable; inserting them between auxiliary and participle does not affect participle agreement. AI-generated, unverified.

value: Plural nouns require plural agreement of determiners and adjectives (les livres intéressants).
The plural -s is not pronounced but agreement is marked in writing.

evidence.notes: Plural marking on the noun triggers plural agreement across the noun phrase. AI-generated, unverified.

value: Pourvu que is invariable; the subjunctive verb agrees with its own subject in person and number.
The exclamatory single-clause use does not change subject agreement.

evidence.notes: Pourvu que + subjunctive keeps normal subject agreement (Pourvu qu'il vienne). AI-generated, unverified.

value: Pourvu que is invariable and introduces a subjunctive clause whose verb agrees with its own subject.
The main clause and the pourvu que clause agree independently with their own subjects.

evidence.notes: Two-clause construction: each verb agrees with its own subject. AI-generated, unverified.

value: à is invariable; city names normally take no article, so no gender or number agreement applies.
Cities that do carry an article keep it and agree accordingly (Le Caire, La Havane).

evidence.notes: Article-less city names mean the preposition shows no contraction; the listed exceptions keep their article. AI-generated, unverified.

proposals.entity_key: Preposition with countries: en, au, aux
value: The preposition reflects the country's gender and number: en + feminine or vowel-initial masculine, au + masculine singular, aux + plural.
Contracted forms au (à + le) and aux (à + les) show the country's gender and number.

evidence.notes: Geographic prepositions agree with the gender/number of the country name. AI-generated, unverified.

proposals.entity_key: Preposition with islands: à, aux, en
value: à is used for a single island and aux for plural island groups, reflecting the island's number.
Exceptions with en (en Haïti, en Martinique, en Guadeloupe) show no gender or number marking in the preposition.

evidence.notes: Island usage varies; à/aux track number while the listed en exceptions are fixed. AI-generated, unverified.

proposals.entity_key: Preposition with states/provinces: en, au, dans le
value: The preposition reflects the state's gender and number: en + feminine or vowel-initial masculine, au + masculine.
dans le contains the masculine singular article, so the state's masculine gender is marked explicitly.

evidence.notes: States/provinces follow country-like gender/number rules with the dans le variant. AI-generated, unverified.
